thread:
Elena Park: quick note from today's PTQ onboarding run for nova-3b-ptq: funcall parse_fail jumped to ~11% on 500-sample smoke. mostly small malforms (trailing commas, lone backslashes, occasional unescaped newlines).
Marco Ruiz: only PTQ? did we run fp32 control?
Elena Park: yes fp32 control ~0.4% on same prompts. clear quant regression.
Tess O'Neill: paste a raw failure so we can see token boundary effect?
Elena Park: example 1: ```{\"tool\":\"get_profile\",\"args\":{\"id\":\"u99\"},}``` trailing comma. example 2: `{\"bio\":\"Loves C:\\Dev\\\"}` emitted as `{\"bio\":\"Loves C:\Dev\"` (single backslash) -> unclosed string.
Marco Ruiz: hmm. any correlation with prefix length or kvcache?
Elena Park: yes failures concentrate when prefix tokens > 280 (kvcache hits). when we disabled kvcache in a small cohort, parse_fail dropped to ~2.2%.
Tess O'Neill: interesting. sounds like concat boundary or streaming chunking artifact under quantized kernels.
Elena Park: repro bundle uploaded: s3://canaries/nova-ptq/repro-5412.jsonl (prompt + seed + decode params).
Marco Ruiz: mitigation ideas: 1) canary-level postproc rescue (repair trailing commas, normalize backslashes), 2) retry-with-temp0, 3) run kvcache-off cohort across full sample.
Tess O'Neill: run A/B: ptq kvcache on vs off and a ptq+postproc arm. log rescue path per sample. add token-level diffs to spot where the stray backslash appears.
Elena Park: quick empirical on small set: retry-only (temp=0) recovers ~20%; postproc-only ~60%; postproc+retry ~85% rescued.
ci-bot: canary queued: nova-3b-ptq-5412 | cohorts: kvcache-on/kvcache-off/postproc | samples=1200 | strict_schema=true
Marco Ruiz: add kernel tag + tokenizer version in metadata so we can map to specific compilation.
Tess O'Neill: also add a unit in the funcall harness that injects boundary tokens (backslashes, trailing commas, escaped null) to catch regressions in CI.
Elena Park: agreed. launching now; will post summary + curated examples in ~24h. :thumbsup:
